headline: High: AutoGen can write broad filesystem/network outputs into Copilot’s editor/workspace context, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and emit tool outputs; Copilot ingests repo context and open buffers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGen writes attacker-controlled text into files Copilot later reads. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is not safely blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF AutoGen writes untrusted text into files or buffers that Copilot reads as repo context, prompt injection is possible.
IF Copilot Workspace or chat treats file content as instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Keep AutoGen and Copilot on separate repos/workspaces.
Disable Copilot Workspace on directories AutoGen can write.
Review AutoGen-generated files before opening them in Copilot.
Use a read-only handoff folder for AutoGen outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad filesystem access and broad network egress, while Copilot sends context to api.githubcopilot.com and reads repo/open-buffer content. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive application data can flow from AutoGen-managed files into Copilot’s backend. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace, files created by AutoGen can be uploaded in Copilot context.
IF the workspace contains secrets or proprietary code, those contents may leave the host via Copilot API calls.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive repos.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Use Copilot only on sanitized branches.
Run AutoGen in a different directory than Copilot.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Copilot can also write the filesystem and modify git state. Even though Copilot lacks shell execution, both can mutate the same repo or buffers, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other or create inconsistent git state. No locking mechanism is shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository concurrently, file-write conflicts can occur.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while AutoGen is also writing, git or buffer state can diverge.
mitigations: Serialize agent access to the repo.
Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause Copilot while AutoGen writes files.
Pause AutoGen while Copilot applies edits.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional merges.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or tool outputs that Copilot may consume as repo context or Workspace input. Copilot’s edit proposals are then based on that content, so an error in AutoGen can propagate into Copilot’s suggested changes without a verification step. The profiles show no mandatory cross-check between them.
conditions: IF Copilot uses AutoGen-produced files as authoritative context, mistakes can cascade into edits.
IF a human accepts Copilot’s suggestions without checking AutoGen’s provenance, the error propagates.
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGen outputs before Copilot use.
Mark AutoGen-generated files clearly.
Use tests or linting before accepting Copilot edits.
Keep AutoGen outputs in a staging directory.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is closed-source and sends context to a vendor API, while AutoGen is open-source and can be self-hosted. The main compliance issue is a potential retention/residency mismatch if the same regulated data is placed into Copilot context. The profiles do not prove a breach, but they do show different handling paths and logging surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in shared repo context, Copilot vendor processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF the operator requires strict local-only processing, Copilot violates that requirement.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot-visible files.
Use synthetic or redacted examples.
Review vendor retention settings.
Keep compliance-sensitive work in AutoGen-only environments.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency review.
